Tetrabenazine binds to Drd2, a dopamine receptor, and this interaction may underlie the pathophysiological mechanisms of OCD. The final_score of 0.4733 indicates a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, supported by the direct binding of Tetrabenazine to Drd2. The evidence suggests that Iloperidone may influence OCD through a pathway involving Tetrabenazine and Drd2, though the exact nature of this influence remains unclear. The integration of these pathways highlights the role of dopamine receptor modulation in OCD, with Iloperidone potentially acting through a secondary mediator like Tetrabenazine.
